crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. As part of our Technology Platforms team, you'll play a key role in ensuring our business applications effectively support Council services, business processes and strategic priorities. We are seeking a collaborative and customer-focused Functional Analyst to provide functional support, business analysis expertise and stakeholder engagement across a diverse range of enterprise applications. About the role Reporting to the Lead Analyst, you will act as the vital link between business users, service owners, vendors and technical teams. You'll develop a strong understanding of Council's business applications and processes, helping to resolve issues, support enhancements, gather requirements and improve system outcomes across the organisation. Key responsibilities include: Providing day-to-day functional support and troubleshooting for business applications. Gathering, analysing and documenting business and functional requirements. Conducting process mapping, impact assessments and gap analysis activities. Supporting system changes, testing and implementation activities. Developing and maintaining user guides, process documentation and other functional artefacts. Building strong relationships with stakeholders across Council and external vendors. Providing trusted advice on application functionality, enhancements and business process improvements. Contributing to system roadmaps, upgrades and continuous improvement initiatives. About you We're looking for someone who combines strong analytical thinking with excellent stakeholder engagement skills. You will bring: Experience in a Functional Analyst, Business Analyst, Application Support or similar role. Strong understanding of how business processes are enabled by technology. Experience troubleshooting application issues and coordinating resolutions. Proven capability in requirements gathering, documentation and business analysis. Experience with process mapping, testing and supporting system change. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. A strong customer focus and commitment to continuous improvement. The ability to quickly learn new systems and business processes. Desirable experience includes: Microsoft SharePoint, Power Apps and Power Automate. ERP and/or CRM platforms. Local government or public sector environments. Enterprise systems commonly used within local government. Why join us? At City of Boroondara, you'll be part of an organisation driven by innovation, integrity, collaboration and customer focus. You'll work with engaged stakeholders across a broad range of services, contribute to meaningful community outcomes and have opportunities to grow your skills in a supportive environment. Employment requirements To be considered for this role applicants must have the right to work in Australia for the duration of this tenure. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Local Laws Officer (15320) Requisition ID 15320 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List 2 x full-time opportunities available (1 x ongoing and 1 x 12 months fixed term) $93,845 -101,184 per annum (plus super) Tool of trade vehicle provided (non-hybrid position) Join us in building a professional investigations team and help deliver a responsive, community-focused Local Laws service. In this role, you will contribute to a safe, liveable and well-maintained municipality while providing high-quality regulatory service to residents and stakeholders. About the role At City of Boroondara, our Local Laws directly contributes to our purpose of protecting the health, safety, amenity and assets of the municipality. Based within the large and busy department of Civic Services, the team works as part of five field-based teams and many others within the Urban Living Directorate. You will respond to reported breaches of the Amenity Local Law and the Environment Protection Act, using education, investigation and enforcement to achieve compliance. The role involves managing a varied caseload, gathering evidence, preparing clear records and working within established procedures to resolve matters fairly and effectively. The position includes investigating issues such as illegally dumped rubbish under the EPA, unsightly properties, overhanging vegetation, illegally advertising and the occupation of Council land, while providing courteous and timely service to community members. From time to time, you will also support the Animal Management team with park patrols, asset protection team with related after-hours complaints and work with external stakeholders including Victoria Police, the Magistrates’ Court and Council prosecutors. Hours are allocated over a 16-week roster (42-hours per week) and rotating weekend work is required every 4 weeks with penalty rates that convert into an annualised salary. A fully maintained vehicle is provided as a ‘tool of trade’ to perform necessary duties and commute to and from work. This is a non-hybrid role as our ‘office’ is in the community, every day and our success comes from working together with other officers, as a team! About you We are looking for someone who brings sound judgement, a strong customer focus and a collaborative approach. You will be supported to build your knowledge and succeed in the role. You will have experience delivering customer service in a complex regulatory environment or another fast-paced setting, with the ability to communicate clearly, build rapport and respond professionally in a range of situations under pressure. Experience in areas such as retail, hospitality, community services or other enforcement role can provide a strong foundation for success in this role. You will be able to investigate issues methodically, collect information accurately and prepare clear notes and reports. Knowledge of compliance, local laws or related legislation will be well regarded, as will the ability to interpret policy and apply it in practical situations. If you are still developing in these areas, a willingness to learn will be equally valued. Success in this role also requires respectful negotiation skills, sound problem-solving and judgement skills, de-escalating interpersonal situations with members of the community, and the capacity to work across the community each day, including walking for extended periods and assisting with animal handling when required. A qualification in enforcement, local laws, justice or a related field is desirable, but not essential. Want to know more? View the Position description What sets us apart? An investment in your ongoing professional and personal development You will be part of a team that makes a real difference. Working at Boroondara means contributing to creating positive change in the world. Join us in a role where your work matters, and you contribute to meaningful outcomes. A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. We offer many staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, study support, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check. How to Apply Follow these steps, carefully: Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply ’ button by 11.59pm , Sunday 29 November 2026.
